frozen_hypothesis.canonical_wording: Can pre-treatment and early-treatment physiological information predict a specific post-VSS failure phenotype, rather than generic treatment failure, early enough to change the salvage decision?

options: R2-C3 (headache despite normal ICP + improved papilledema + no restenosis)
prediction_target.current_status: The target is to predict WHICH of these 5 phenotypes will develop, not just binary success/failure
prediction_target.key_distinction_from_2026_lit: Lakhani 2026 predicts binary readmission; Maroufi 2026 compares treatment arms. Neither predicts within-arm failure TYPE.

prediction_time.requirement: Before failure manifests — i.e., at pre-treatment or early-treatment stage
prediction_time.current_status: The hypothesis requires prediction BEFORE failure. This is the key temporal constraint.

exact_variables_NOT_yet_defined: baseline opening pressure (available in some cohorts)
venous pressure distribution (SSS, torcula, TS, SS, JB — available in D'Amato protocol)
post-stent pressure evolution (NOT available in open data)
ICP waveform (NOT available in open data)
headache phenotype per ICHD-3 (NOT available in any VSS cohort)
CGRP biomarker (NOT available in any VSS cohort)
BMI / weight trajectory (available in some cohorts)
inputs.warning: The CEO directive states: 'The machine should not bundle these together and call the combination a primitive.' Each input must be individually justified. The exact combination has NOT been defined because no open dataset has all of them.

decision.proposed_decision: IF predicted failure type = R2-C1 → plan for CSF shunt salvage; IF R2-C2 → plan for re-stenting; IF R2-C3 → plan for headache-directed treatment (CGRP antagonist, migraine prophylaxis); IF R2-C4 → plan for optic nerve sheath fenestration; IF R2-C5 → symptomatic management
decision.key_question: Does this decision differ from what clinicians already do?

technical_effect.what_materially_improves: UNKNOWN — not yet demonstrated. The hypothesis claims that knowing failure TYPE in advance changes the salvage pathway. But this has NOT been shown to improve outcomes, reduce time to salvage, reduce complications, or reduce cost.

decision_matrix.question: Does failure-type prediction actually change decisions, or do existing clinicians already choose actions according to these phenotypes?

matrix.existing_practice_already_does_this: PARTIALLY — when ICP is elevated post-VSS, clinicians already escalate to shunt. But they do so REACTIVELY (after failure occurs), not PROACTIVELY (before failure). The proposed system would predict R2-C1 BEFORE it manifests, allowing pre-emptive planning.
matrix.decision_value: MODERATE — pre-emptive planning could reduce time-to-salvage but does NOT change the salvage treatment itself

matrix.existing_practice_already_does_this: YES — when angiographic restenosis is found, re-stenting is standard practice. Clinicians already do 6-month angiography to detect this.
matrix.decision_value: LOW — the proposed system would predict restenosis before it occurs, but the treatment (re-stenting) is the same. The only value is earlier detection, which routine angiography already provides.

matrix.predicted_failure: R2-C3 (headache despite normal ICP + improved papilledema + no restenosis)
matrix.proposed_action: Headache-directed treatment (CGRP antagonist, migraine prophylaxis, behavioral therapy)
matrix.existing_practice_already_does_this: NO — current practice does NOT identify R2-C3 as a distinct phenotype. When headache persists post-VSS, clinicians typically: (a) repeat LP to check ICP, (b) repeat angiography to check restenosis, (c) if both normal, offer symptomatic treatment without a specific headache-directed pathway. The proposed system would PRE-IDENTIFY patients who will develop R2-C3, allowing early headache-directed intervention.
matrix.decision_value: HIGH — this is the one phenotype where pre-treatment prediction would change the decision. Instead of offering VSS and then discovering headache persists, the system would redirect R2-C3-prone patients to headache-directed treatment BEFORE VSS.

matrix.existing_practice_already_does_this: PARTIALLY — when visual loss progresses despite controlled ICP, ONSF is considered. But this is reactive. Pre-emptive ONSF planning could reduce time-to-intervention.
YES — symptomatic management is default practice

decision_matrix_summary.key_finding: The decision-value of failure-type prediction is CONCENTRATED in R2-C3. For R2-C2 and R2-C5, existing practice already covers the decision. For R2-C1 and R2-C4, the value is moderate (pre-emptive vs reactive). ONLY R2-C3 offers a genuinely different decision pathway (headache-directed treatment vs VSS).
decision_matrix_summary.implication: The invention frontier, IF IT EXISTS, is specifically about predicting R2-C3 — not about predicting 'failure type' in general. The broad 'failure-type prediction' framing is too wide. The NARROWED target should be: 'Can pre-treatment information predict R2-C3 specifically, early enough to redirect the patient away from VSS toward headache-directed treatment?'

Lakhani_2026.what_info_they_use: Presenting symptom phenotype (visual-only, headache-only, visual+other, mixed/nonvisual) from Nationwide Readmissions Database ICD codes
Lakhani_2026.what_they_predict: IIH-related inpatient readmission within 300 days (binary); repeat intervention (binary)
Lakhani_2026.what_decision_they_influence: 'Individualized risk stratification and symptom-specific counseling when selecting patients for VSS' — i.e., whether to offer VSS
what_they_CANNOT_do: Cannot predict failure TYPE (R2-C1 vs R2-C2 vs R2-C3 vs R2-C4 vs R2-C5)
Cannot distinguish R2-C3 from R2-C1 (both present as 'headache-only')
Cannot use physiological measurements (ICP, gradient, venous distribution)

Maroufi_2026.what_info_they_use: Obesity (binary) × visual disturbance (binary) = 4 phenotypes; TriNetX EHR data
Maroufi_2026.what_they_predict: Persistent headache, papilledema, visual disturbance at 24 months (binary outcomes per phenotype); retreatment; ED visits
Maroufi_2026.what_decision_they_influence: VSS vs ventricular shunting selection by phenotype — 'VSS preferable in nonobese without visual symptoms; VS better for papilledema in obese without visual disturbance'
what_they_CANNOT_do: Cannot predict within-arm failure TYPE (only compares arms)
Cannot distinguish R2-C3 from R2-C1 within headache outcome
Cannot use ICHD-3, CGRP, or venous manometry
Cannot predict individual patient outcome (only group-level comparative effectiveness)

cumulative_gap_after_adversarial_analysi.what_2026_lit_ESTABLISHES: Broad phenotype → binary outcome (readmission, headache, papilledema, visual disturbance)
cumulative_gap_after_adversarial_analysi.what_2026_lit_does_NOT_establish: Phenotype + physiology → specific failure TYPE (R2-C1/C2/C3/C4/C5) → salvage decision
cumulative_gap_after_adversarial_analysi.narrowest_remaining_gap: Can pre-treatment information distinguish R2-C3 (headache despite normal ICP + improved papilledema + no restenosis) from R2-C1 (headache + elevated ICP)? Both present as 'headache-only' in Lakhani's framework. This is the ONE distinction that would change the salvage decision.
